author: fester
body: A read of a file on a target that has no filesystem. There is no block driver behind these calls on arm64, so the honest answer is to refuse the compile and say which call cannot be served. Answering the empty string instead is what this reports: the caller named a path, got "", and could not tell that apart from an empty file. `run.ps1` fails the build on the tag, so the refusal is a compile error and not a warning somebody reads later.

author: fester
body: The write path is deliberately NOT here. `write-file` answers 0, which the callers already read as failure -- `fs-layer` prints "<write failed>" on this lane and is telling the truth. Only the reads lie.

author: fester
body: The builtin-List pattern intrinsics, refused for a third reason: they are not implemented on this lane and there is no honest value to answer with. A `when` on a builtin List desugars to a length test plus __list-head and __list-tail over an O(1) tail view, and none of the three exists in the arm64 runtime.

author: fester
body: Refusing is the honest answer while the intrinsics are unimplemented. The arms match on the name alone, no arity gate, so a partial application refuses too. codex/test/list-pattern.cross-refusal pins that the refusal fires; lose these arms and that test compiles clean and the row goes red.
